body: Laminated cards, one each, and the trainer hands them round. Ten past two on a Tuesday in a function room over a carvery, and eleven people from a housing association are getting their results back. A man of fifty-one, twenty-nine years in repairs and about eighteen months off retiring, reads his four letters twice and then reads the paragraph underneath, and says, to nobody, that is me, that is exactly me. He is not being sarcastic. He puts the card in his shirt pocket rather than his folder, and at the break he takes it out again while the kettle is going and reads the bit about how he handles conflict.

What pleased him was not the psychology. It was being described accurately by something that had no reason to flatter him, at fifty-one, by name, in a room where he is usually the man who fixes doors. He had been seen.

Identity has become an enormous cultural category, and nearly all of what it now carries is descriptive. It is the set of traits, preferences and histories that make a person distinguishable, arrived at by examination — tests, types, reflection, the long project of working out who you really are underneath.

The biblical usage runs in the opposite direction, and it is easy to miss because the word is the same. Adopted. Named. Bought. Grafted in. Take the last one literally for a moment, because it is horticulture before it is theology. A graft contributes nothing to its own grafting. The cut is made in the other tree. The wound is on the other tree. The branch is held in place by somebody with a knife until the join takes, and afterwards it lives on sap that it did not produce and cannot manufacture, drawn up through a root system it has never seen. Nothing about the branch changed. Everything about what it is attached to did.

The dial runs from HM 300.30 to HM 398.70 and carries 121 stations, of which 46 are on air today. HM 384.20 is Identity in Yeshua, assigned and in build and not yet on air, with Sons and Daughters at seven in the morning and Authority Walk at seven in the evening in its published schedule and no audio behind them yet.

Set the two accounts side by side and the difference is not one of emphasis. One of these is discovered by looking inward and describing what is there. The other is conferred, from outside, by somebody else. The second sort cannot be self-administered, and that is the expensive part. You cannot give it to yourself in a quiet moment, you cannot work up to it, and no amount of effort applied to your own interior will produce it, which means the whole apparatus most people have for improving themselves is simply the wrong tool and cannot be adapted.

It is worth being fair about why the descriptive account won, because it did not win by trickery. It is useful. Teams work better when people know how the others are wired. It gave language to a great many people who had none, and it got a generation out of a religion that told them their inner life was mostly to be suppressed. But a description is only as good as the reporting, and it has to be maintained: re-tested, defended, updated when it stops fitting. That is exhausting, which is why so much of the culture built on it is anxious. Anything you must keep verifying, you are never done verifying.

This band makes the same distinction in an engineering key, which is less inspiring and more useful. A station holds its frequency permanently. It does not hold it because it performs, and it cannot lose it by performing badly. The smallest service on the dial keeps its number on exactly the same terms as the flagship, and no station is ever asked to re-earn a number it already has. A frequency is not a reward for listening figures. It is a commitment made once, from outside, by somebody with the authority to assign it.
There is one more thing to say about the descriptive account, and it is not that it is false.

Everything the personality frame reports may be perfectly accurate. The man with the laminated card really does handle conflict that way; his wife could have told the trainer for nothing. The difficulty is not accuracy, it is jurisdiction. A description tells you what is currently there and has no authority to say what should be. And it fails precisely when it is needed most, because the instrument and the subject are the same person. On the week you cannot get out of bed, self-examination reports that you are somebody who cannot get out of bed, with total confidence, and has no way of knowing it is out of calibration. You are asking a broken gauge whether it is broken.
A verdict you issue about yourself is not a verdict.

A woman of thirty-four is sitting on a bench in a corridor at the county court on a Wednesday morning with a boy of four who is running a fire engine along the edge of the seat and making the noise for it. They were told half past ten and it is nearly eleven. He has a cough he has had since Christmas. When they are called the whole thing takes about eleven minutes, and the court has a teddy bear that lives in a drawer for the photograph, and the boy is more interested in the drawer. On the way home he falls asleep before they are out of the town. She stops for petrol, and standing at the pump in the cold she thinks this is an absurd thing to be doing at this precise moment, and does it anyway.

Nothing about the boy changed in those eleven minutes. Same cough, same fire engine. Everything about where he stands changed, and none of it happened inside him, or can be revised by anything he later finds out about himself.

The honest cost is that the conferred account is harder to feel, and pretending otherwise helps nobody. A description gives you something to check. A status conferred years ago gives you nothing to check on a bad Tuesday but the bare fact that it was done, which can feel like being handed a receipt. Introspection is the only instrument most people were ever taught to use, and this account tells them it does not reach. That lands as cold, and calling it cold is not unreasonable.

But the thing you cannot feel is the thing that holds. Any status you could verify by feeling would fail on the days you most needed it, because feeling is the first thing to go. The boy asleep in the back is not adopted in proportion to how adopted he feels; when he is seventeen and furious and says something he will regret, the order does not soften. That is the whole advantage, and it is only available to a status that was never yours to issue.

So the claim is stronger and stranger than the therapeutic version, and it should not be smoothed into it. It says that the most important true thing about a person is not something they found out about themselves. It is not their type, their gifting, their wiring, their story or their diagnosis, none of which are false and none of which are load-bearing. It is a standing that somebody else established, at cost, and recorded, and does not intend to revisit.
All of which is argument, and argument stays theory until something is actually playing.

Four kinds of programming run on this dial, and it helps to know they are there before you start turning. Most of the band is music — praise and worship, gospel, country, hymns and a good deal besides. There is teaching and prayer, where the Word is opened and prayed through rather than sung. There is family programming, which is simply safe to have on in a room with children in it. And there are the international stations, hosted in their own languages rather than translated into them afterwards. The teaching frequencies sit together in their own stretch of the band, which is where the station on this subject will open when it opens.

Until then, start at HM 304.80 — Celebrate Yeshua! It is biblical music in the contemporary style, and it earns the recommendation on the article’s own terms in two ways. The songs are Scripture-rooted, which means what is being sung over you is what the text says about you rather than what you have worked out about yourself; the words came from outside the room, as the status did. And the station is named for the one doing the conferring rather than the one receiving it, which is a small thing until you notice how much religious music is named the other way about. It runs Morning CCM at eight and drive-time in the late afternoon, and none of it is tailored to your type.

There is nothing to install. No app, no download and no card — open kJubilee.com on whatever phone or laptop is nearest and press play. It is deliberately built for inexpensive phones and thin connections, so it starts on the hardware people actually have. If you want it nearer to hand, add the page to your home screen and it will open like anything else on it. And do make yourself an account while you are there. It keeps your favourites with you across every Jubilee site, and it is how the band learns which frequencies people are really reaching for — which is how the next one gets built.

Take that as an invitation rather than an exercise. Put HM 304.80 on tomorrow morning while you are getting dressed, on a day you have no particular feeling about yourself one way or the other, and let it say the same things it would have said on your best week. You do not have to agree with it, and you certainly do not have to feel it. It was not waiting for either.
